discrepancies.topic: Program name in the notes vs the source file

a.value: 'You can run this code with python chat.py'

discrepancies.note: w71-n03 shows the official code verbatim and says the file in the source code is chat3.py; run it as `python chat3.py` after downloading.

discrepancies.topic: Week topics missing from the notes' Summing Up

a.value: topic line includes System Prompt, User Prompt, Reinforcement Learning, Explore vs. Exploit, Neural Networks, Transformer Architecture, Hallucinations

b.value: Summing Up lists 8 items without those

discrepancies.note: All of them are taught in the notes' body; the package covers every topic of the week page.

a.value: 'a board where the computer wins as 1 and one where the computer loses as -1'; 'The computer will attempt to win by maximizing its own score'

b.value: X winning scores 1, O winning scores -1, a tie 0; X maximizes and O minimizes

discrepancies.note: Same algorithm described from two viewpoints; w71-n05 uses the lecture's X/O convention and says so.

a.value: 'Machine learning is a way by which a computer can learn through reinforcement.'

b.value: 'reinforcement learning is one way to think about this ... a type of machine learning'

discrepancies.note: w71-n06 presents reinforcement learning as one kind of machine learning, alongside supervised learning in w71-n07.

discrepancies.topic: Terms in the notes that the lecture does not say

a.value: the notes use 'embeddings' and attribute the 2017 attention paper to Google; the minimax section uses 'tic-tac-toe'

b.value: the transcript has no 'embedding'; it describes a word as 'an array or vector of numbers' (1,536 floats) and shows recent papers without naming Google

discrepancies.note: Both kept: the notes' term in Persian with the English term, and the lecture's description marked «از سخنرانی».

a.value: 'unsupervised learning is a means by which the AI can learn with minimal human intervention'

b.value: official transcript: 'We've got to move to an Supervised model.'

discrepancies.note: Likely a transcription slip for 'unsupervised'; the package follows the notes.

discrepancies.topic: Speller in the AI source code

a.value: src/speller/ contains the Problem Set 5 distribution code (dictionary.c with TODO stubs, speller.c, Makefile, dictionary.h)

b.value: the notes mention Copilot but not Speller

discrepancies.note: Not reproduced. The lecture shows Copilot implementing check and load; the package only describes the demonstration and never includes an implementation (FORBID71, D84).

discrepancies.topic: 'This was CS50!' in the middle of the course

b.value: in the 2026 course order the AI lecture comes after Week 7 (SQL) and before Week 8

discrepancies.note: The lecture was recorded as a special lecture with family members in the audience; the app places week-ai between week 7 and week 8 (site number 71).
